# Pleats

> Pleats is a fabric stash app for iPhone: a sewing inventory and project planner for people who sew. It keeps a fabric stash with lengths, checks the stash before you buy, plans projects against it, and adds up what a make really cost (fabric by the length used, notions, the pattern and logged hours). In beta; free during the beta. Made by one developer, Ekaterina Baliasnikova.

Key facts:
- Platform: iPhone only (iOS 18 or later). No account, no sync: data stays on the device.
- Free plan: up to 30 fabrics, 10 notions, 5 patterns and 3 active projects.
- Pleats+: $19.99/year with a 14-day free trial, $2.99/month, or $49.99 once. Adds unlimited items, line-by-line cost, suggested sale price, Lock Screen timer, stats and CSV export.
- Contact: support@plts.app

Every page is also available as Markdown: request it with `Accept: text/markdown`, or add `.md` to the path.

## Pages

## Guides

- [Sewing guides](https://plts.app/guides.md): index of all guides
- [How much fabric do I need for a dress?](https://plts.app/guides/how-much-fabric-for-a-dress.md): rough amounts by style and fabric width; estimating yardage from your own measurements, with a worked example
- [How much does fabric shrink?](https://plts.app/guides/fabric-shrinkage.md): typical first-wash shrinkage for cotton, linen, viscose, wool, silk, synthetics and knits; testing a piece; prewashing
- [How to price handmade clothes](https://plts.app/guides/pricing-handmade-clothes.md): materials, time and overheads; markup, margin or hourly rate, with a worked example

- [How to keep a fabric stash inventory](https://plts.app/guides/fabric-stash-inventory.md): what to record for each fabric, keeping it current, spreadsheet vs app
- [Do I have enough fabric for this pattern?](https://plts.app/guides/enough-fabric-for-a-pattern.md): reading a yardage chart by size and width; shrinkage, nap, one-way prints, plaid matching; metres and yards
- [How to work out what a sewing project cost](https://plts.app/guides/sewing-project-cost.md): fabric by length used, notions, pattern and hours, with a worked example; markup vs margin
